checks.title: PREADY only in an APB Access cycle
checks.behavior: At every rising edge of i_clk_core with i_rst_n_core=1: if o_apb_pready=1, then i_apb_psel=1 and i_apb_penable=1 at the same edge.

checks.title: PREADY is a one-cycle pulse
checks.behavior: If o_apb_pready=1 at rising edge N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N and N+1, then o_apb_pready=0 at edge N+1.

checks.title: PSLVERR only with PREADY
checks.behavior: At every rising edge and also while i_rst_n_core=0: if o_apb_pslverr=1, then o_apb_pready=1 at the same edge.

checks.title: PRDATA holds its value outside the PREADY cycle
checks.behavior: If i_rst_n_core=1 at rising edges N-1 and N, and o_apb_pready=0 at edge N, then o_apb_prdata at edge N equals o_apb_prdata at edge N-1. In other words, o_apb_prdata changes value only at an edge where o_apb_pready=1 is sampled, or through reset.

checks.title: Legal Setup launches channel A in the first Access cycle (early launch)
checks.behavior: Checker model: apb_busy is set to 0 by i_rst_n_core=0. It is set to 1 at an edge where SETUP holds and cleared to 0 at an edge where o_apb_pready=1. SETUP(N) means that at rising edge N: i_rst_n_core=1, i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0 and apb_busy=0. This includes the edge directly after an o_apb_pready=1 edge with i_apb_psel held at 1. LEGAL(N) means i_apb_paddr[1:0]=2'b00 and (i_apb_pwrite=0 or i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111) at N. Property: if SETUP(N) holds, then o_apb_pready=0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0 at N. If SETUP(N) and LEGAL(N) hold and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then at edge N+1: o_tlul_a_valid=1, o_apb_pready=0 and o_apb_pslverr=0.

checks.title: Channel A payload equals the captured APB request
checks.behavior: If SETUP(N) and LEGAL(N) hold (see CHK-005) and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then at edge N+1: o_tlul_a_opcode = 3'b100 if i_apb_pwrite@N=0, or 3'b000 if i_apb_pwrite@N=1. o_tlul_a_address[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] = i_apb_paddr@N[PARA_ADDR_W-1:2] and o_tlul_a_address[1:0]=2'b00. If i_apb_pwrite@N=1, then o_tlul_a_data = i_apb_pwdata@N, bit for bit.

checks.title: Illegal Setup gives a local error in the first Access cycle with no TL-UL request
checks.behavior: If SETUP(N) holds and LEGAL(N) does not, that is i_apb_paddr[1:0]!=2'b00 or (i_apb_pwrite=1 and i_apb_pstrb!=4'b1111) at N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then at edge N+1: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1, o_apb_prdata=32'h0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0.

checks.title: A request is raised only after a legal Setup
checks.behavior: If i_rst_n_core=1 at edges N and N+1, o_tlul_a_valid=0 at edge N and o_tlul_a_valid=1 at edge N+1, then SETUP(N) and LEGAL(N) held at edge N. So o_tlul_a_valid never rises at any other time, including after illegal requests, orphan responses or while apb_busy=1.

checks.title: Channel A held and stable until accepted
checks.behavior: If o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=0 at rising edge N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at N and N+1, then at edge N+1: o_tlul_a_valid=1, and o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address, o_tlul_a_data, o_tlul_a_param, o_tlul_a_size, o_tlul_a_mask, o_tlul_a_source and o_tlul_a_user equal their values at edge N.

checks.title: o_tlul_a_valid drops after the handshake (one request per transfer)
checks.behavior: If o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1 at rising edge N, and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then o_tlul_a_valid=0 at edge N+1.

checks.title: At most one TL-UL request outstanding, only inside an APB transfer
checks.behavior: Checker model: OUTST is set to 0 by reset. It is set to 1 at an edge with o_tlul_a_valid=1, i_tlul_a_ready=1 and i_tlul_d_valid=0. It is cleared at an edge with i_tlul_d_valid=1 and OUTST=1. Property: at every rising edge with i_rst_n_core=1, if o_tlul_a_valid=1, then OUTST=0 and apb_busy=1 (see CHK-005). Also, OUTST=1 implies apb_busy=1.

checks.title: Constant channel A fields and legal opcode encoding
checks.behavior: At every rising edge, and also while i_rst_n_core=0: o_tlul_a_param=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID, o_tlul_a_user=0 (all PARA_A_USER_W bits), o_tlul_a_opcode[1:0]=2'b00, o_tlul_a_address[1:0]=2'b00, and o_tlul_a_opcode is either 3'b000 or 3'b100. It is never 3'b001 (PutPartialData) or any undefined value.

checks.title: Accepted TL-UL response is mapped to the APB completion in the next cycle
checks.behavior: RESP(N) means that at edge N, with i_rst_n_core=1 and o_tlul_d_ready=1: i_tlul_d_valid=1 and (OUTST=1 or (o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1)). RD means i_apb_pwrite=0 at the last SETUP edge. ERR = i_tlul_d_error=1, or i_tlul_d_opcode != (RD ? 3'b001 : 3'b000), or i_tlul_d_source != PARA_SRC_ID, all sampled at N. Property: if RESP(N) holds and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then at edge N+1: o_apb_pready=1 and o_apb_pslverr=ERR. o_apb_prdata = i_tlul_d_data@N if RD=1 and ERR=0, and o_apb_prdata=32'h0 otherwise (any write, and any error).

checks.title: PREADY only as the result of an illegal Setup or an accepted response
checks.behavior: If o_apb_pready=1 at edge N+1 and i_rst_n_core=1 at N and N+1, then at edge N either (SETUP(N) holds and LEGAL(N) does not), or (RESP(N) holds and apb_busy=1). So there is no completion without a response (no timeout) and no second completion per transfer.

checks.title: Orphan response has no APB effect
checks.behavior: ORPHAN(N) means that at edge N: i_rst_n_core=1, i_tlul_d_valid=1 and RESP(N) is false (OUTST=0 and not (o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=1)). If ORPHAN(N) holds, the edge N is not an illegal SETUP, and i_rst_n_core=1 at N+1, then at edge N+1: o_apb_pready=0, o_apb_pslverr=0 and o_apb_prdata equals its value at edge N. The OUTST model state is not changed by the orphan.

checks.title: Output values while reset is asserted
checks.behavior: Whenever i_rst_n_core=0, checked at every rising edge and on every change of i_rst_n_core to 0 after a delta delay (no clock edge needed): o_tlul_a_valid=0, o_tlul_d_ready=0, o_apb_pready=0, o_apb_prdata=32'h0, o_apb_pslverr=0, o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b000, o_tlul_a_address=0 and o_tlul_a_data=32'h0.

checks.title: o_tlul_d_ready is 1 from the first edge after reset release
checks.behavior: If i_rst_n_core=1 at rising edges N-1 and N, with no reset assertion between them, then o_tlul_d_ready=1 at edge N. Equivalently, the reset value 0 is seen only at the first edge after release, and the value is 1 at every later edge until reset is asserted again.

checks.title: Power-on and asynchronous reset behaviour
checks.behavior: Check the reset values, the asynchronous assertion and the d_ready release timing with all checkers active.
checks.stimulus: Hold i_rst_n_core=0 for 5 cycles with the inputs idle (i_apb_psel=0, i_tlul_d_valid=0). Release it synchronously, just after a rising edge of i_clk_core. Run a legal write so that o_tlul_a_data, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_opcode become non-zero (use a read for the opcode). Then, in the middle of a clock cycle (between edges), during A1 and during the PREADY cycle, drive i_rst_n_core=0 for 3 cycles and release it synchronously again.
checks.expected: While i_rst_n_core=0: o_tlul_a_valid, o_tlul_d_ready, o_apb_pready, o_apb_pslverr=0, o_apb_prdata=0, o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b000, o_tlul_a_address=0 and o_tlul_a_data=0. They go to 0 before the next rising edge after the mid-cycle assertion. The constants are o_tlul_a_param=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_a_user=0, also during reset. o_tlul_d_ready=0 at the first edge after release and 1 from the second edge on. No PREADY or o_tlul_a_valid appears after release until a new Setup.

checks.title: Aligned full-strobe write to a prompt device
checks.behavior: Directed write, CFG-BASE. Check the PutFullData conversion and the 3-cycle Access phase.
checks.stimulus: Setup cycle S: i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0, i_apb_pwrite=1, i_apb_pstrb=4'b1111, i_apb_paddr random with [1:0]=2'b00, i_apb_pwdata random. Then i_apb_penable=1, with the inputs held until o_apb_pready. The device drives i_tlul_a_ready=1 in the first cycle o_tlul_a_valid=1 (A1). In the next cycle (A2) it drives i_tlul_d_valid=1, i_tlul_d_opcode=3'b000, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID, i_tlul_d_error=0 and i_tlul_d_data random non-zero. Repeat for 50 random address and data values.
checks.expected: In S: o_apb_pready=0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0. In A1: o_tlul_a_valid=1, o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b000, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111, o_tlul_a_address=PADDR, o_tlul_a_data=PWDATA, o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID and o_tlul_d_ready=1. Exactly one A handshake. In A3: o_apb_pready=1 with o_apb_pslverr=0 and o_apb_prdata=0. The Access phase lasts exactly 3 cycles (2 wait states).

checks.title: Aligned read, PSTRB ignored
checks.behavior: Directed and random reads. Check the Get conversion, the returned data and that PSTRB is ignored.
checks.stimulus: Run reads (i_apb_pwrite=0) to aligned i_apb_paddr, cycling i_apb_pstrb through all 16 values including 4'b0000, with random i_apb_pwdata. The device is prompt: i_tlul_a_ready=1 in A1, then in A2 i_tlul_d_valid=1, i_tlul_d_opcode=3'b001, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID, i_tlul_d_error=0 and i_tlul_d_data random.
checks.expected: For every PSTRB value: o_tlul_a_opcode=3'b100, o_tlul_a_size=2'b10, o_tlul_a_mask=4'b1111 and o_tlul_a_address=PADDR in A1. Exactly one request. In A3: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=0 and o_apb_prdata=i_tlul_d_data. The Access phase lasts 3 cycles. There is no difference in behaviour between PSTRB values.

checks.title: Write with unsupported PSTRB is rejected locally
checks.behavior: Directed writes using each of the 15 strobe values other than 4'b1111. Each is followed directly by a legal transfer.
checks.stimulus: Run aligned writes with i_apb_pstrb set to each value in {4'b0000..4'b1110}. The device would answer promptly if asked. After each one, start the next Setup in the cycle right after o_apb_pready: a legal aligned write with PSTRB=4'b1111.
checks.expected: For each illegal write, in the first Access cycle: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=0 (Access phase of 1 cycle, no wait state). o_tlul_a_valid stays 0 for the whole transfer, so there is no TL-UL request. The following legal write is accepted in the cycle after PREADY (Setup-to-Setup interval 2) and completes normally, as in CHK-019.

checks.title: Misaligned read or write is rejected locally
checks.behavior: Directed misaligned reads and writes, each followed directly by a legal transfer.
checks.stimulus: For i_apb_paddr[1:0] in {2'b01, 2'b10, 2'b11}, run reads (any PSTRB) and writes (PSTRB=4'b1111 and also other values). Follow each one with a legal aligned read in the cycle after o_apb_pready.
checks.expected: In the first Access cycle: o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=0 (1 Access cycle). o_tlul_a_valid=0 throughout, so there is no TL-UL request. The next Setup is accepted in the cycle after PREADY and the legal read completes correctly.

checks.title: Device d_error response
checks.behavior: Directed read and write, each answered with d_error=1.
checks.stimulus: Run a legal aligned read and a legal aligned write with a prompt device. The device response has i_tlul_d_error=1, the correct i_tlul_d_opcode (3'b001 for read, 3'b000 for write), i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and i_tlul_d_data=32'hFFFFFFFF.
checks.expected: Each transfer issues exactly one request and completes in the 3rd Access cycle with o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=32'h0. The next transfer is unaffected (no stored error).

checks.title: Wrong d_opcode or wrong d_source response
checks.behavior: Directed responses with a bad opcode or a bad source, in CFG-BASE and CFG-NARROW.
checks.stimulus: Run legal reads answered with each i_tlul_d_opcode != 3'b001 (3'b000 and 3'b010..3'b111), and legal writes answered with each i_tlul_d_opcode != 3'b000 (3'b001..3'b111). In both cases i_tlul_d_error=0, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and i_tlul_d_data non-zero. Then run reads and writes answered with the correct opcode and d_error=0 but i_tlul_d_source != PARA_SRC_ID: in CFG-BASE (PARA_SRC_ID=0) use d_source=1 and 8'hFF; in CFG-NARROW (PARA_SRC_ID=1) use d_source=0. Also run the d_error, opcode and source combinations together.
checks.expected: Every case completes with o_apb_pready=1, o_apb_pslverr=1 and o_apb_prdata=32'h0, in the cycle after the response. Control runs with the correct opcode and source complete with o_apb_pslverr=0.

checks.title: Channel A back pressure and response delay
checks.behavior: Constrained-random a_ready and d_valid delays.
checks.stimulus: Run random legal reads and writes. The device holds i_tlul_a_ready=0 for D cycles of o_tlul_a_valid=1, with D random in 0..8, then asserts it for one cycle. It answers R cycles after the acceptance cycle, with R random in 0..6, where R=0 means the same cycle. In 10% of transfers, i_tlul_a_ready toggles between transfers while o_tlul_a_valid=0.
checks.expected: While o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=0, o_tlul_a_opcode, o_tlul_a_address and o_tlul_a_data stay unchanged. Exactly one handshake per transfer. The Access phase length is D+R+2 cycles. Completion values follow CHK-013. The scoreboard matches.

checks.title: Orphan responses are discarded
checks.behavior: Inject d_valid pulses when no request has been accepted.
checks.stimulus: Drive i_tlul_d_valid=1 for one cycle, with random d_opcode, d_source, d_error and d_data: (a) while the APB side is idle (i_apb_psel=0); (b) in the Setup cycle; (c) while o_tlul_a_valid=1 and i_tlul_a_ready=0 (before acceptance); (d) in the PREADY cycle and in the cycles after the real response. After each one, run a legal read and a legal write with a prompt device. The TL-UL device-side checker is relaxed for these injected responses.
checks.expected: An orphan never produces o_apb_pready=1, never sets o_apb_pslverr, and does not change o_apb_prdata. In case (c), the transfer still waits for the real response after acceptance and completes with the real response's values. The following transfers complete correctly, with nominal timing and data.

checks.title: Same-cycle response shortens the Access phase
checks.behavior: Directed: the device answers in the acceptance cycle.
checks.stimulus: Run legal reads and writes. In A1 the device drives i_tlul_a_ready=1 and, in the same cycle, i_tlul_d_valid=1 with the correct opcode, i_tlul_d_source=PARA_SRC_ID and i_tlul_d_error=0 (random d_data for reads).
checks.expected: o_apb_pready=1 in A2: the Access phase is 2 cycles (1 wait state). o_apb_pslverr=0. o_apb_prdata=d_data for reads and 0 for writes. Exactly one request.

checks.title: Reset during a transfer abandons it
checks.behavior: Directed reset in A1, A2 and A3.
checks.stimulus: For each phase A1 (o_tlul_a_valid=1, before acceptance), A2 (accepted, waiting for the response) and A3 (the cycle with o_apb_pready=1), assert i_rst_n_core=0 asynchronously for 3 cycles. Reset the APB Requester and device models at the same time (i_apb_psel=0, no pending response). Release synchronously and wait 20 idle cycles. Then run a legal read and a legal write with a prompt device.
checks.expected: After release there is no o_apb_pready and no o_tlul_a_valid during the 20 idle cycles, so there is no completion for the abandoned transfer. The next read and write complete exactly as in CHK-019 and CHK-020 (3 Access cycles, correct data), showing that both sides are idle.

checks.title: Back-to-back transfers with PSEL held high or with idle gaps
checks.behavior: Check every ordered pair of transfer kinds and the minimum Setup-to-Setup interval.
checks.stimulus: Run every ordered pair (X,Y) of {legal write, legal read, illegal-strobe write, misaligned access}, for each device mode {prompt (accept A1, respond A2), same-cycle response, prompt with d_error=1}. Mode 1: i_apb_psel stays 1 and the Setup of Y is driven in the cycle right after o_apb_pready of X (only i_apb_penable drops to 0). Mode 2: i_apb_psel=0 for G cycles in between, with G=1 and G=5. Also run long constrained-random sequences of all kinds with random gaps 0..5, in CFG-BASE and CFG-NARROW.
checks.expected: Every transfer completes in order with its own correct o_apb_pslverr and o_apb_prdata, matched by the scoreboard. No TL-UL request is made for illegal transfers. At most one request is outstanding. The Setup-to-Setup interval when X is a legal transfer with a prompt device, with or without d_error, is 4 cycles; with a same-cycle response it is 3; when X is illegal it is 2. With G idle cycles the interval is the same value plus G. The bridge never adds an idle cycle.

checks.title: Random end-to-end scoreboard and coverage closure
checks.behavior: Constrained-random regression with a scoreboard that compares each TL-UL request and each APB completion with the APB transfer that caused it.
checks.stimulus: Run random aligned reads and writes with random data and addresses, mixed with illegal-strobe and misaligned requests. Use random a_ready delays 0..8, d_valid delays 0..6 or same-cycle, random injected d_error, wrong opcode and wrong source, orphan pulses, and random APB gaps including PSEL held high. Use CFG-BASE and CFG-NARROW over several seeds, recording each seed.
checks.expected: Every legal APB transfer produces exactly one TL-UL request with matching opcode, address and data, and exactly one APB completion with the expected o_apb_pslverr and o_apb_prdata. Illegal transfers produce no request. All bins are hit: COV-001 (all 16 PSTRB values on writes, reads with PSTRB zero and non-zero); COV-002 (d_error, wrong opcode, wrong source, illegal strobe and misaligned, each on read and write); COV-003 (a_ready waits 0..8 and d_valid delays 0..6 plus same-cycle); orphan timing; and back-to-back ordered pairs.

checks.title: PPROT and unused D-channel inputs have no effect
checks.behavior: Run the same transfer sequence with different values on the ignored inputs and compare.
checks.stimulus: Run a fixed sequence of legal reads and writes, and illegal requests, twice. First with i_apb_pprot=3'b000 and i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user all 0. Then with i_apb_pprot random per transfer (all 8 values) and i_tlul_d_param, i_tlul_d_size, i_tlul_d_sink and i_tlul_d_user random on every response.
checks.expected: Both runs give the same cycle-accurate values on all outputs: o_tlul_a_* fields, o_tlul_a_valid, o_apb_pready, o_apb_pslverr and o_apb_prdata.

checks.title: No response from the device: the transfer waits indefinitely
checks.behavior: The device accepts the request but never answers.
checks.stimulus: Run a legal read. The device asserts i_tlul_a_ready in A1 and then keeps i_tlul_d_valid=0 for 1000 cycles, with the Requester holding the Access phase. Then assert reset (bridge, Requester and device together), release, and run a legal write.
checks.expected: For the 1000 cycles, o_apb_pready=0, o_apb_pslverr=0 and o_tlul_a_valid=0 after the handshake cycle. There is no timeout completion. After reset the legal write completes normally.

checks.title: Legal parameter configurations
checks.behavior: Build and run a basic traffic test with each legal configuration, with all assertion groups bound.
checks.stimulus: Configurations: CFG-BASE (defaults). CFG-NARROW (PARA_ADDR_W=16, PARA_SRC_W=1, PARA_SRC_ID=1). An extreme configuration (PARA_ADDR_W=32, PARA_SRC_W=8, PARA_SRC_ID=255, PARA_A_USER_W=32, PARA_D_SINK_W=4, PARA_D_USER_W=32). For each, run random legal reads and writes with all-ones and random high address bits, and responses with d_source=PARA_SRC_ID.
checks.expected: Each configuration elaborates. o_tlul_a_address equals i_apb_paddr over all PARA_ADDR_W bits, including the MSB. o_tlul_a_source=PARA_SRC_ID. o_tlul_a_user is 0 on all PARA_A_USER_W bits. Responses with d_source=PARA_SRC_ID complete with o_apb_pslverr=0. Any other d_source gives o_apb_pslverr=1.

checks.title: Illegal parameter values are reported at elaboration
checks.behavior: Elaboration sweep of the verification source set.
checks.stimulus: Elaborate with each illegal value, one at a time: PARA_ADDR_W=15 and 33; PARA_SRC_W=0 and 9; PARA_SRC_ID=2 with PARA_SRC_W=1, and 256 with PARA_SRC_W=8; PARA_A_USER_W=0 and 33; PARA_D_SINK_W=0 and 5; PARA_D_USER_W=0 and 33. Also elaborate with the boundary legal values 16, 32, 1, 8, 2^PARA_SRC_W-1, 1 and 32, 1 and 4, and 1 and 32.
checks.expected: Every illegal value causes an elaboration error message and a failed elaboration (it is not silently clamped). Every boundary legal value elaborates without error.

assumptions: Checker model state is built only from interface signals. apb_busy is set at a Setup edge (i_apb_psel=1, i_apb_penable=0, apb_busy=0) and cleared at an edge with o_apb_pready=1. OUTST is set by an A handshake with no same-cycle d_valid and cleared by a d_valid while OUTST=1. RD is ~i_apb_pwrite at the Setup edge. These model the spec's FSM states (IDLE/BUSY/DONE, REQ/WAIT) as seen from the ports.

The APB Requester model follows APB4: one Setup cycle, i_apb_penable=1 in Access, and request signals stable until o_apb_pready. Synchronous reset release is provided by the testbench. Without this, CHK-001 and CHK-005 are not meaningful.

The TL-UL device model returns one response per accepted request with d_source=PARA_SRC_ID, except in tests that deliberately inject orphan, wrong-opcode or wrong-source responses. For those, the device-side TL-UL protocol checker is relaxed.
o_tlul_a_data is compared with i_apb_pwdata only for writes, because the spec says it is unused by the device on Get.
CFG-NARROW is taken as PARA_ADDR_W=16, PARA_SRC_W=1, PARA_SRC_ID=1. The spec only states PARA_SRC_ID=1 for CFG-NARROW.

A response with a wrong d_opcode to an accepted request completes with PSLVERR=1 (DEC-008, REQ-ERR-004). It is not silently discarded. The TL-UL library's host 'discard wrong-opcode' statement is applied to orphans only.
Timing statements such as 'at edge N' refer to values sampled at the rising edge of i_clk_core. An output registered at edge N is observed at edge N+1.
